questions.question: How does adverse selection impact market efficiency in both the insurance / and used car markets?
questions.solution_html:
• Impact of adverse selection in market efficiency in both the insurance and used car
  • markets- Adverse selection occurs when one agent in a transaction knows about a
  • hidden characteristic of a good and decides whether to participate in the transaction
  • on the basis of this (private) information. In insurance market, high-risk individuals
  • are more likely to buy insurance, while low-risk individuals may avoid it due to high
  • premiums. This leads to higher costs for insurers, forcing them to raise prices or limit
  • coverage, reducing overall market efficiency. In used car market, sellers know more
  • about a car’s condition than buyers. If buyers fear purchasing a defective car (a
  • "lemon"), they may offer lower prices, discouraging sellers of high-quality cars from
  • participating. This results in a market dominated by low-quality vehicles, reducing
  • trade volume and efficiency.
  • marks for briefly stating the concept and its impact on the specified markets, give
questions.final_answer: marks for briefly stating the concept and its impact on the specified markets, give

questions.question: Explain briefly the different methods of calculating national income.
questions.solution_html:
• Different methods of calculating national income- Income Method – The approach
  • sums up all earnings generated in an economy, including wages, rent, interest, and
  • profits. Expenditure Method – The method calculates national income by adding up
  • all spending on final goods and services, including consumption, investment
  • government spending, and net exports (exports minus imports). Product (Value
  • Added) Method – The method measures national income by calculating the total value
  • of goods and services produced in various sectors, subtracting the cost of intermediate
  • goods to avoid double counting.
questions.final_answer: goods to avoid double counting

questions.question: How does adverse selection impact market efficiency in both the insurance / and used car markets?
questions.solution_html:
• Impact of adverse selection in market efficiency in both the insurance and used car
  • markets- Adverse selection occurs when one agent in a transaction knows about a
  • hidden characteristic of a good and decides whether to participate in the transaction
  • on the basis of this (private) information. In insurance market, high-risk individuals
  • are more likely to buy insurance, while low-risk individuals may avoid it due to high
  • premiums. This leads to higher costs for insurers, forcing them to raise prices or limit
  • coverage, reducing overall market efficiency. In used car market, sellers know more
  • about a car’s condition than buyers. If buyers fear purchasing a defective car (a
  • "lemon"), they may offer lower prices, discouraging sellers of high-quality cars from
  • participating. This results in a market dominated by low-quality vehicles, reducing
  • trade volume and efficiency.
